page.overview:
What is Adventure?

Adventure is an unreleased theme, presumed to be an Adventurers subtheme or reboot intended for release in 2005.

This cancelled Adventure theme appears to consist of two subthemes, each comprised of five sets. Their set numbers begin with 7425, immediately succeeding the Orient Expedition set 7424 Black Cruiser, and end with 7472, immediately preceding the Dino Attack set 7473 Street Sprinter vs. Mutant Lizard. The first subtheme, encompassing sets 7425-7428 and 7430, is themed around Egypt, much like 1998's Desert. The second subtheme, encompassing sets 7431-7434 and 7472, is themed around dinosaurs, much like 2000's Dino Island. Both subthemes share recurring minifigures that appear to be updated variants of Johnny Thunder and Dr. Kilroy, confirming that they are part of a single theme. They also both share dark red or earth green vehicles with similar aesthetics, such as the classic Adventurers parts 30149 and 30147. At least within the Egypt sets, the heroes use dark red vehicles and the villains use earth green vehicles, which parallels bright red being associated with the heroes in Dino Island and Orient Expedition as well as combining the villains' use of bright blue in Dino Island and bright yellow in Orient Expedition.

The set inventories suggest that both Adventure subthemes would have released in 2005. For example, the Egypt set 7425 includes motorcycle elements with part IDs 50859, 50861, and 50862 that all made their debut in 2005 City sets, while the Dino set 7472 T-Rex Trouble includes part ID 50933 that is introduced in the 2005 BIONICLE set 8740 Toa Hordika Matau. but was confirmed to have been cancelled by early 2005.

Although some information about this cancelled Adventure theme had been known by Lowlug and Eurobricks forums users in early 2005, most details were unknown until LEGO data could be accessed through BrickLink's Inventory Comparison Tool in 2024-2025, allowing these sets to be documented on theqelement; this oversight was eventually patched in December 2025, preventing BrickLink users from accessing cancelled set inventories. The LEGO Group has yet to publicly comment on these sets, aside from Greg Farshtey once mentioning the behind-the-scenes history of Dino Attack on BZPower.
